notes: Threads operating choices for the resident worker. These are our own editorial/operational choices, not Meta limits.
Timezone is NOT defined here. It is read from operations_policy.json (the same setting C8 and C9.5 use).

Windows are [start, end) in the operations timezone. They say when something MAY happen, never when it MUST happen: 07:00 means publication may become eligible from 07:00, not that a post goes out at 07:00.
The daily activity target is ADVISORY. It is not a quota, a health condition, a hard minimum or a hard maximum. More than the upper bound is not an error; there is deliberately no hard daily cap.
Human approval means 'this content may be published'. It does not mean 'publish now'. Selection and timing are separate decisions.
T4.1 is PLAN-only: automatic publication is disabled in code, not only here.
T4.2: approval requests are batched into ONE digest email. Each proposal in a digest keeps its own review session and its own approve/reject decision; there is no approve-all.
T4.2: approval TTL starts when the request is actually sent, never when the proposal was generated. Nighttime generation does not consume the TTL.

approval_notification_flush.note: Evaluates whether a digest is due. Sending also requires the worker to be started with --send-approval-digests.

queue.evidence: ordering uses explicit facts only; insight metrics are not ranking evidence in T4.1

approval_digest.note: cooldown = minimum spacing between digests; gather = how long the first request-worthy proposal may wait so later ones can join the same email. A full digest (max_items ready) does not wait for gather, only for cooldown.

stock.note: Advisory coverage of approved-but-unpublished proposals, in days of the advisory daily target. Not a quota: above the high mark new approval requests are deferred, never deleted.
